evidence: Concrete sequence: hydration A creates seat S and adds relationship R; grouped provenance records created/reused seat IDs (DESIGN-NOTES.md:285-286,302). A later, independently selected hydration B reuses S and R without changing a field, which the design permits case by case (DESIGN-NOTES.md:39-40,285-286). The stated inverse for A retires objects A created and reverses relationships A added (DESIGN-NOTES.md:286; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:47-48). Applied literally, it retires S and removes R despite B's continuing use, contradicting the requirement that undo preserve unrelated later work (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:47; DESIGN-NOTES.md:279,287-289). Same-field edit conflict handling does not catch this dependency because B made no edit. Exact dependency conflict checks are acknowledged as unfinished (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:49; DESIGN-NOTES.md:274,289). The finding concerns the missing later-reuse rule, not a claim that the draft implementation already loses state.
